claims.text: A tailored dual-step thermo-mechanical treatment can induce coherent nanoprecipitates in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The induced precipitates will be uniformly distributed and approximately 10–20 nm in size.
The precipitate-forming treatment will enhance yield strength.
The precipitate-forming treatment will enhance tensile ductility.
The treatment will preserve high-temperature stability.
The treatment will preserve irradiation stability.
The initial refractory high-entropy alloy has a high-temperature-stable, irradiation-resistant matrix.
The initial alloy has suboptimal mechanical performance.
Controlling aging temperature and duration during dual-step processing will control coherent nanoprecipitate formation.
The treated microstructure and its mechanical benefits will remain effective at 800 °C and above.
The treated microstructure will remain effective under irradiation typical of nuclear or aerospace applications.
Nanoscale precipitates strengthen the alloy by pinning dislocations.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations associated with premature crack initiation.
Coherent nanoprecipitation can provide high strength and tensile ductility simultaneously in tungsten refractory high-entropy alloys.
The precipitate treatment will not trigger phase instabilities that compromise thermal or irradiation resistance.
Relative to the untreated alloy, the treated alloy will show increased yield strength and ductility.
Maintaining precipitate size near 10–20 nm and preserving coherency are necessary for the proposed benefits.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency could compromise alloy stability under extreme conditions.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant strength and ductility enhancement relative to the control is a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The stated baseline is an untreated alloy, whereas the proposed experiment compares the dual-step treatment with a conventional heat treatment. These are not necessarily the same control condition.
